newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: PLO asks for U.N. council action on Israeli building.
newsitem.headline: PLO asks for U.N. council action on Israeli building.

text.p: The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) called on Monday for action by the Security Council in response to Israel's reaffirmation of its decision to build new Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.

The PLO's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, said Israel reiterated its intention to proceed with the plan less than 24 hours after the General Assembly adopted a resolution last Thursday by an overwhelming majority calling on it to refrain from all actions or measures, including settlement activities, which alter the facts on the ground.

At issue is a plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem, called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians, that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war.
In identical letters to Secretary-General Kofi Annan and council president Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland, al-Kidwa did not specifically request a Security Council meeting.
But he said the "present serious situation created by Israel's intransigence, as well as its flagrant challenges to the international community, necessitate action by the Security Council."

"We do hope that this time, under the current circumstances, the council will be enabled to exercise its responsibilities under the Charter of the United Nations," he said, alluding to the fact the United States vetoed a council resolution March 7 similar to the one later adopted by the Assembly, where there is no veto.

"We call upon the Security Council to do so and to specifically demand immediate and full cessation of all Israeli settlement activities in the occupied Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem, especially the settlement in Jabal Abu Ghneim," al-Kidwa added.
An Israeli official said in Jerusalem late on Monday that surveyors would start working on the site on Tuesday.
